s: A company has many AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The accounts contain many Amazon EC2 instances that run different types of workloads. The workloads have different usage patterns. The company needs recommendations for how to rightsize the EC2 instances based on CPU and memory usage during the last 90 days. Which combination of steps will provide these recommendations? (Select THREE.)
o: Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer and enable trusted access for Compute Optimizer for the organization.
Configure a delegated administrator account for AWS Systems Manager for the organization.
Use an AWS CloudFormation stack set to enable detailed monitoring for all the EC2 instances.
Install and configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all the EC2 instances to send memory utilization metrics to CloudWatch.
Activate enhanced metrics in AWS Compute Optimizer.
Configure AWS Systems Manager to pass metrics to AWS Trusted Advisor.
x: Compute Optimizer looks back 14 days by default. A 90-day window needs enhanced infrastructure metrics (E), plus organization opt-in (A) and the CloudWatch agent for memory (D). 'Systems Manager passes metrics to Trusted Advisor' (F) isn't a real integration.

w.y: AWS Compute Optimizer gives rightsizing recommendations across an organization once opted in with trusted access. By default it analyzes 14 days; enhanced infrastructure metrics extend the lookback to three months (about 93 days). Memory is not a default EC2 metric, so the CloudWatch agent must publish it for Compute Optimizer to use.

o.A: Correct: opting in at the management account with trusted access covers all member accounts.
o.B: A Systems Manager delegated administrator has nothing to do with Compute Optimizer recommendations.
o.C: Detailed (1-minute) monitoring changes granularity, not the lookback window, and does not provide memory metrics.
o.D: Correct: the CloudWatch agent publishes memory utilization, which Compute Optimizer then analyzes.
o.E: Correct: enhanced infrastructure metrics extend the lookback period from 14 days to three months.
o.F: Systems Manager does not feed metrics to Trusted Advisor, and Trusted Advisor is not the 90-day CPU/memory rightsizing tool.

s: New for AWS Compute Optimizer – Enhanced Infrastructure Metrics to Extend the Look-Back Period to Three Months
